instrument: Action Plan for Plant-based Foods (Ministry of Food, Agriculture and Fisheries)
target_text: Six pillars: value chain, sales, export, crops and ingredients, food base, research. Protein from green biomass to 'reduce dependence on soya imports'
metric: none quantified for production or consumption
funding: Plant-based Food Grant DKK 675 M for 2023 to 2030 (about DKK 84 M or USD 12 M a year); later reported as DKK 812 M; made permanent in 2024 (EUR 55 M cited)
achieved_so_far: No KPIs or evaluation framework in the plan; outcomes not measurable from published data
lessons: Money plus a permanent fund without a numeric goal; cannot be judged against a target
notes: Retail plant-based sales DKK 32 bn (2021) as context; 15 protein crops named as suitable

instrument: Green Tripartite agreement: CO2e tax on livestock
target_text: Tax on livestock emissions from 2030; land conversion by 2045
metric: tax rate per t CO2e before and after 60% basic deduction
value: DKK 300 (2030) and 750 (2035) headline; DKK 120 and 300 effective
funding: Green Area Fund DKK 40 bn; plant-based grant made permanent
achieved_so_far: Agreed June 2024; tax not yet in force (starts 2030); 250,000 ha forest and 140,000 ha peatland by 2045
lessons: First livestock carbon price anywhere; paired with transition money and a phase-in with deductions
notes: WRI cites an agriculture reduction aim of 55 to 65% by 2030 (not verified in primary text)

instrument: National Protein Strategy (Ministry of Agriculture)
target_text: Raise self-sufficiency in new protein sources and protein crops over 5 to 10 years; indicative track shares (legumes about 20%, novel about 20%, insects about 15%, circularity about 20%, diet about 15%, sustainable soy about 5%)
value: n/a (about 80% of vegetable protein imported in 2020)
achieved_so_far: No official quantitative targets or calculations published; 2024 government reframed animal protein as 'indispensable' for security
lessons: Technology-led 'promissory' strategy that avoided export livestock questions; weak measurement; politically reversible
notes: Critique from peer-reviewed geography (Boterman 2026)

instrument: Consumption ambition within the protein strategy
target_text: Shift from 60% to 50% animal-sourced protein in Dutch diets
achieved_so_far: Not tracked in sources read
lessons: Consumption ratio goals are easy to state and hard to measure; out of scope for a Vietnamese supply vision
notes: Demand-side; included as benchmark only

instrument: Regional protein strategy
target_text: 60% plant and 40% animal protein by 2030
achieved_so_far: not read
lessons: Same measurement issue as the Dutch goal
notes: Advocacy report citation only

instrument: Protein Crop Strategy (Eiweisspflanzenstrategie)
target_text: Ecosystem services, regional value chains, more domestic non-GMO protein
funding: EUR 6 M a year from 2016; GFI 2026: EUR 5 M protein diversification plus a share of EUR 67 M
achieved_so_far: Pulses 191,700 ha in 2018 after CAP greening counted legumes on ecological focus areas
lessons: Area moved when CAP payment rules changed, not because of the strategy budget
notes: No self-sufficiency target

instrument: National Food Strategy (independent review, 'The Plan')
target_text: Diet and food-system recommendations (numbers not read this wave)
achieved_so_far: Government response (2022) not read
lessons: Independent reviews without adoption leave no targets to track
notes: Gap: numbers and government response not verified

instrument: Report on the development of plant proteins in the EU, COM(2018)757
target_text: Identify measures to raise competitiveness of EU protein crops
achieved_so_far: High-protein feed self-sufficiency about 26% (FEFAC, undated) and 25.8% (2025)
lessons: A plan without a number produced no measurable change in seven years
notes: Total feed protein self-sufficiency about 76 to 78%

instrument: Action Plan for resilience, strategic autonomy and sustainability of the EU protein system, COM(2026)355
target_text: EU-origin share of protein from oilseeds and protein crops used as feed rises from 25.8% (2025) to 35% (2035)
metric: share of feed protein from EU-grown oilseeds and protein crops
funding: CAP post-2027, European Competitiveness Fund, Horizon Europe (over EUR 190 M previously), EIB
achieved_so_far: New (July 2026); baseline 74% of high-protein feed and 94% of soya imported
lessons: First numeric feed-protein target at EU level; framed as resilience and strategic autonomy; adds a harmonised protein balance sheet and an EU-wide benchmark
notes: Names precision and biomass fermentation, algae and insects (feed) among sources; Commission fermentation study due H2 2026

instrument: Protein Industries Canada sector roadmap (plant-based food, feed and ingredients)
target_text: CAD 25 bn additional annual sales; 10% of global plant-based food market
funding: PIC federal CAD 150 M for 2023 to 2028 (about USD 22 M a year); PIC plus industry 'nearly half a billion dollars' since 2018 (claim)
achieved_so_far: No published baseline or progress report against the target found
lessons: Industry-led supercluster with a headline number but no interim milestones or measurement
notes: Includes feed

instrument: Israel Innovation Authority national operational plan for alternative proteins
target_text: Keep R&D and future manufacturing in Israel; public fermentation scale-up infrastructure
value: USD 2.5 bn and 10,000 jobs by 2030 (IIA, WEF and GFI Israel report, 2024)
funding: Over NIS 230 M foodtech grants in a decade, over NIS 140 M in alternative protein, about 90% since 2020
achieved_so_far: 73 start-ups and about 10% of global alt-protein VC 2014 to 2023 (report claims)
lessons: R&D-led niche strategy; projection co-authored by an advocacy group
notes: Projection is a claim, not a target

instrument: '30 by 30' (Singapore Food Story)
target_text: Produce 30% of nutritional needs locally by 2030
funding: S$144 M R&D programme (2019) and later calls (v0.1)
achieved_so_far: Dropped Nov 2025; achieved about 26% for protein (eggs and seafood) and 8% for fibre
lessons: Land, cost and finance constraints beat the target; alt protein excluded 'in the short term' for cost and acceptance
notes: Replaced by Food Story 2

instrument: Singapore Food Story 2
target_text: 30% of protein (eggs and seafood) and 20% of fibre produced locally
funding: S$42 M for 11 future-food projects (nine on alternative protein)
achieved_so_far: New
lessons: Regulator, R&D and finance role kept; production role narrowed
notes: Alternative protein outside the food-security targets

instrument: 1st Basic Plan for Fostering the FoodTech Industry (under the Food Tech Industry Promotion Act)
target_text: Five-year plan: funds, clusters, regulation improvement, sandbox for by-product upcycling
value: KRW 51 bn (2024) to 81 bn (2026) to 100 bn (2027); centres 7 to 10 by 2030
funding: KRW 100 bn cumulative by 2027 (about USD 68 M)
achieved_so_far: New (July 2026)
lessons: Statute plus five-year basic plans gives a review cycle; no alternative-protein volume target
notes: Press sources; primary plan not read

instrument: Food security targets (major crops) and feed-grain policy
target_text: Major-crop self-sufficiency 55.5%; milling wheat 5% by 2025; food corn 2% by 2027; KRW 1 M per ha to switch rice to corn
achieved_so_far: Milling wheat 5% 'difficult to achieve'; compound feed about 22.1 Mt a year (MY2023/24) still import-based; DDGS 5.6% of feed
lessons: A feed-importing economy of Vietnam's feed size sets food-crop, not feed-protein, targets
notes: USDA GAIN interpretation

instrument: Basic Plan for Food, Agriculture and Rural Areas (2020)
target_text: Feed self-sufficiency 25% (FY2018) to 34% (FY2030); calorie self-sufficiency 37% to 45%; feed rice 430 kt to 700 kt
achieved_so_far: Pure-domestic feed self-sufficiency 26 to 28% in FY2018 to FY2024 and 24% (FY2025 est.); target cut to 28%
lessons: Land-based feed self-sufficiency barely moved in 25 years (26% in FY2000, 26% in FY2024)
notes: Baseline definitions differ (25% vs 27% for FY2018); see disagreements

instrument: First Basic Plan under the revised Basic Act (2025)
target_text: Calorie self-sufficiency 38% (FY2023) to 45% (FY2030); pure-domestic feed self-sufficiency 28% (FY2030); annual KPI checks (PDCA)
achieved_so_far: Feed-rice area fell 53% in one year (98,666 ha FY2024 to 46,004 ha FY2025); calorie ratio 37% (FY2024)
lessons: Annual public verification makes misses visible; feed crops compete with food rice when rice is short
notes: Concentrate feed self-sufficiency only 10 to 13% since 2000

instrument: MIDORI Strategy for Sustainable Food Systems
target_text: Zero fossil CO2 in agriculture, forestry and fisheries; chemical pesticide risk minus 50%; chemical fertiliser minus 30%; organic 1 Mha (25% of farmland); 100% artificial seedlings for eel and bluefin tuna
achieved_so_far: not assessed this wave
lessons: A 2050 food-system vision with a few hard KPIs; no protein or feed-protein KPI
notes: Alternative protein not in the page read

instrument: Food-tech investment roadmap (press report)
target_text: Public plus private investment JPY 9.7 tn to 2040, of which novel foods JPY 1 tn; 30% shares for plant factories and land-based aquaculture
achieved_so_far: New
lessons: Long horizon but market-share framing; primary not read
notes: Press only

instrument: MARA action plan to cut soybean meal in feed (2023; earlier 2021 plan)
target_text: Soybean-meal share of feed below 13% by 2025 and 10% by 2030 (about 17% in 2017)
achieved_so_far: 13.4% in 2025 (official, target missed); about 16% in 2024 (USDA and industry)
lessons: Formulation lever moves faster than land (minus 0.14 to 0.45 pp a year) but the 2030 target needs minus 0.68 pp a year
notes: Full treatment in GEO; benchmarked only

instrument: Future food strategy under BCG (NXPO)
target_text: Future food exports THB 140 bn to THB 350 bn by 2027
achieved_so_far: not verified
lessons: Export-value framing; conflicting target figures in circulation
notes: GFI cites a market-value goal of THB 500 bn by 2027

instrument: Aquaculture feed policy goals (salmon)
target_text: All aquaculture feed from sustainable sources by 2030; more Norwegian raw materials (no number found)
achieved_so_far: Marine share 90% (1990), about 30% (2013), 22.4% (2020); Norwegian-origin 8.3% and novel ingredients 0.4% (8,126 t) in 2020
lessons: Price moved marine share down fast; policy has not moved domestic origin or novel ingredients
notes: Aquafeed analogue for Vietnam

instrument: Feed scheme Decision 1625/QD-TTg; no protein strategy
target_text: Industrial livestock feed 30 to 32 Mt; domestic feed additives 30 to 35% of demand
funding: VND 1,310 bn for 2023 to 2030 (about USD 6 M a year)
achieved_so_far: 2025 feed target probably missed (about 21.5 Mt in 2024)
lessons: Only protein-adjacent quantified target; no protein-balance indicator exists
notes: Official targets stop at 2030 (NTS headline 1)
